intro: Convert degrees Celsius (°C) to Fahrenheit (°F) accurately for weather forecasts, clinical body thermometers, baking ovens, and industrial kilns. Using the exact deg C to Fahrenheit formula, multiply Celsius by 9/5 (1.8) and add 32—so water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F), normal body temperature is 37 °C (98.6 °F), and water boils at 100 °C (212 °F). Scan weather, oven, and kiln temperatures from -40 °C to 1,600 °C below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Thermometer Point vs. Interval (ΔT) & Mental-Math Shortcut Drift
items: Converting a specific temperature reading requires adding 32 (°F = °C × 1.8 + 32), whereas converting a temperature change (ΔT, like a 10 °C rise) uses only the 1.8 ratio (Δ10 °C = Δ18 °F, no +32).

The simple Celsius to Fahrenheit conversion shortcut (double °C and add 30) stays within ~2 °F for weather between 10 °C and 30 °C, but drifts heavily at baking temperatures (240 °C gives 510 °F by shortcut vs. 464 °F exact).

faqs.question: What is the deg C to Fahrenheit formula?
faqs.answer: Multiply the Celsius temperature by 9/5 (or 1.8) and add 32: °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32. Each 1 °C step equals a 1.8 °F increase.

faqs.question: What are 0 °C and 100 °C in Fahrenheit?
faqs.answer: 0 °C (freezing point of water) equals exactly 32 °F, and 100 °C (boiling point of water at sea level) equals exactly 212 °F. Both scales meet at -40 °C = -40 °F.

faqs.question: What are 130 °C, 176 °C, and 240 °C in Fahrenheit?
faqs.answer: 130 °C equals 266 °F, 176 °C equals 348.8 °F (350 °F baking oven), and 240 °C equals 464 °F.

faqs.question: Is there a simple Celsius to Fahrenheit conversion shortcut?
faqs.answer: For quick weather estimates between 10 °C and 30 °C, double the Celsius number and add 30 (for example, 20 °C ≈ 70 °F vs. 68 °F exact). For baking, fevers, or science, always use the exact × 1.8 + 32 formula.
